459	def _validate_inputs(bundle: object, trust: object) -> tuple[str, object]:
460	    """Structural validation of bundle and trust.
461	
462	    Returns ``(source, candidate)`` where ``candidate`` is the raw candidate
463	    value (a bare block list or an export-format object carrying ``blocks``).
464	    The bundle itself is never mutated: the signature covers it verbatim.
465	    """
466	    if not isinstance(bundle, dict):
467	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
468	    for field in ("source", "expires_at", "response", "candidate", "proofs"):
469	        if field not in bundle:
470	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
471	    source = bundle["source"]
472	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
473	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
474	    if not _is_int(bundle["expires_at"]):
475	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
476	    # The response is itself a JSON object; anything else cannot be checked
477	    # against the recomputed chain descriptor.
478	    if not isinstance(bundle["response"], dict):
479	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
480	    candidate = bundle["candidate"]
481	    blocks_raw = candidate.get("blocks") if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
482	    if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list) or not blocks_raw:
483	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
484	    if not isinstance(bundle["proofs"], list):
485	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
486	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
487	    if signature is not None and (not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature):
488	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
489	    _validate_state_fields(bundle)
490	
491	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
492	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
493	    if not crypto.is_hex64(trust.get("genesis_hash")):
494	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
495	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
496	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
497	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
498	    for name, entry in sources.items():
499	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
500	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
501	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
502	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
503	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
504	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
505	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
506	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
507	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
508	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
509	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
510	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
511	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
512	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
513	    return source, candidate

516	def _validate_state_fields(bundle: dict) -> None:
517	    """Structural validation of the optional account-state extension.
518	
519	    The four state fields are all-or-nothing; when present, ``state_root`` and
520	    ``state_block_hash`` must be 64-char lowercase hex, ``state_height`` a
521	    non-boolean non-negative integer and ``state_proofs`` a non-empty list.
522	    Every item must carry exactly ``{height, proof}`` and every proof document
523	    exactly the eight documented keys with the right JSON types. Only shape
524	    and type are judged here — domain defects (bad hex, negative balances,
525	    illegal directions) are reported later as integrity/proof failures.
526	    """
527	    present = [field for field in STATE_FIELDS if field in bundle]
528	    if not present:
529	        return
530	    if len(present) != len(STATE_FIELDS):
531	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
532	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_root"]):
533	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
534	    if not _is_int(bundle["state_height"]) or bundle["state_height"] < 0:
535	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
536	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_block_hash"]):
537	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
538	    state_proofs = bundle["state_proofs"]
539	    if not isinstance(state_proofs, list) or not state_proofs:
540	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
541	    for item in state_proofs:
542	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"height", "proof"}:
543	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
544	        if not _is_int(item["height"]):
545	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
546	        proof = item["proof"]
547	        if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != _STATE_PROOF_KEYS:
548	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
549	        if not isinstance(proof["account"], str) or not proof["account"]:
550	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
551	        if not _is_int(proof["balance"]):
552	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
553	        transactions = proof["confirmed_transactions"]
554	        if not isinstance(transactions, list) or any(
555	            not isinstance(tx_id, str) for tx_id in transactions
556	        ):
557	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
558	        if not _is_int(proof["index"]):
559	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
560	        if not isinstance(proof["state_root"], str):
561	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
562	        if not _is_int(proof["height"]):
563	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
564	        if not isinstance(proof["block_hash"], str):
565	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
566	        if not isinstance(proof["siblings"], list):
567	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

571	
572	
573	def _authenticate(
574	    bundle: dict, trust: dict, source: str, now: float
575	) -> None:
576	    """Check source trust, every deadline and the optional Ed25519 signature."""
577	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
578	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
579	    source_entry = sources.get(source)
580	    allowlist_expiry = allowlist.get(source)
581	    if source_entry is None and allowlist_expiry is None:
582	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
583	
584	    # All deadlines are checked before any signature work: an expired,
585	    # correctly-signed bundle is still unusable. A source listed in both
586	    # ``sources`` and ``allowlist`` is bound by both deadlines.
587	    if bundle["expires_at"] <= now:
588	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
589	    if source_entry is not None and source_entry["expires_at"] <= now:
590	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
591	    if allowlist_expiry is not None and allowlist_expiry <= now:
592	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
593	
594	    public_key = source_entry.get("public_key") if source_entry else None
595	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
596	    if public_key is not None:
597	        # A keyed source must sign: a missing signature cannot authenticate.
598	        if signature is None:
599	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
600	        if not crypto.verify_signature(
601	            public_key, bundle_signing_digest(bundle), signature
602	        ):
603	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
604	        return
605	    # The source reached this point only through the allowlist (every sources
606	    # entry pins a key). An unsigned allowlisted bundle is therefore accepted;
607	    # a signature with no pinned key to check it against is meaningless.
608	    if signature is not None:
609	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)

613	
614	
615	def _tip_descriptor(blocks: list[Block]) -> dict:
616	    tip = blocks[-1]
617	    return {
618	        "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
619	        "height": tip.height,
620	        "length": len(blocks),
621	        "status": tip.status,
622	    }

624	
625	def _recompute_chain(candidate_raw: list, trust: dict) -> list[Block]:
626	    """Recompute and validate the whole candidate chain from the pinned genesis.
627	
628	    Mirrors the node's own candidate rules except the endowment balance replay
629	    (an offline client holds no balance convention): genesis anchor, heights,
630	    prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures, unique
631	    tx_id-sorted transactions, Merkle roots, block hashes and the
632	    pending-only-at-tip rule. Every field is checked on the *raw* JSON value so
633	    coercions such as ``"1"`` or ``1.0`` heights are rejected outright; such
634	    type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height, non-positive or
635	    non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while recomputation
636	    mismatches stay ``integrity``.
637	    """
638	    blocks: list[Block] = []
639	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
640	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(candidate_raw):
641	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
642	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
643	        height = block_raw.get("height")
644	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
645	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
646	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
647	        status = block_raw.get("status")
648	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
649	        # A height of the wrong type or sign is a field-type defect (input),
650	        # not a chain mismatch: strings, floats and booleans must never be
651	        # coerced into plausible integers before the linkage checks below.
652	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
653	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
654	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
655	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
656	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
657	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
658	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
659	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
660	        if height != position:
661	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
662	        expected_prev = (
663	            GENESIS_PREV_HASH if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
664	        )
665	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
666	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
667	        if position == 0:
668	            # Genesis must be the exact block the client pinned: confirmed,
669	            # empty, and carrying the trusted hash (recomputed below too).
670	            if status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or txs_raw:
671	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
672	            if block_hash != trust["genesis_hash"]:
673	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
674	        elif position < len(candidate_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
675	            # A pending block may only sit at the chain tip.
676	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
677	
678	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
679	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
680	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
681	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
682	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
683	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
684	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
685	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
686	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
687	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
688	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
689	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
690	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
691	            # Same rule as the block height: the raw amount must already be a
692	            # non-boolean positive integer — never a coercible string, float
693	            # or bool — so a domain/type defect is reported as input.
694	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
695	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
696	            if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
697	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
698	            message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
699	            tx_id = crypto.compute_tx_id(message)
700	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
701	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
702	            if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
703	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
704	            if tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
705	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
706	            seen_tx_ids.add(tx_id)
707	            tx_ids.append(tx_id)
708	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
709	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
710	        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
711	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
712	        recomputed = compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root)
713	        if recomputed != block_hash:
714	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
715	        # Parsed only after every raw field has checked out; never trusted for
716	        # the comparison decisions above.
717	        try:
718	            blocks.append(Block.from_dict(block_raw))
719	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
720	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
721	    return blocks

724	def _check_candidate_summary(candidate: object, descriptor: dict) -> None:
725	    """Cross-check an export-format candidate's own tip summary fields.
726	
727	    A bare block list has nothing to check. A five-field export document's
728	    supplied ``tip_hash/height/length/status`` must equal the recomputed tip
729	    descriptor, exactly as the node requires on resubmission.
730	    """
731	    if not isinstance(candidate, dict):
732	        return
733	    for field in DESCRIPTOR_FIELDS:
734	        if field in candidate and candidate[field] != descriptor[field]:
735	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

738	def _check_response(response: dict, descriptor: dict) -> None:
739	    """Every descriptor field present in the response must equal the tip's.
740	
741	    A response carrying none of the descriptor fields cannot be bound to the
742	    recomputed chain at all, so it is rejected rather than vacuously accepted.
743	    """
744	    matched = False
745	    for field in DESCRIPTOR_FIELDS:
746	        if field in response:
747	            matched = True
748	            if response[field] != descriptor[field]:
749	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
750	    if not matched:
751	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

754	def _check_state_anchor(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> None:
755	    """Bind the state extension's anchor to the recomputed candidate chain.
756	
757	    ``state_height`` must name a confirmed candidate block whose hash equals
758	    ``state_block_hash``; an unknown height, a pending block or a hash
759	    mismatch is an integrity failure. Every state-proof item and document
760	    must agree with both anchor heights, the bundle's state root and the
761	    anchor block hash.
762	    """
763	    height = bundle["state_height"]
764	    state_root = bundle["state_root"]
765	    block_hash = bundle["state_block_hash"]
766	    if height >= len(blocks):
767	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
768	    block = blocks[height]
769	    if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or block.block_hash != block_hash:
770	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
771	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
772	        proof = item["proof"]
773	        if item["height"] != height or proof["height"] != height:
774	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
775	        if proof["state_root"] != state_root or proof["block_hash"] != block_hash:
776	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

779	# -- stage 5: proofs ----------------------------------------------------------
780	
781	
782	def _verify_proofs(proofs_raw: list, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
783	    """Validate uniqueness and cross-block consistency of every proof.
784	
785	    Each entry is ``{"height": int, "proof": doc}`` and the proof document
786	    follows the server shape ``{height, tx_id, index, merkle_root, block_hash,
787	    siblings}``. Proofs for the pending tip are forbidden. The verified
788	    transaction ids are returned sorted ascending.
789	    """
790	    verified: list[str] = []
791	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
792	    for item in proofs_raw:
793	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
794	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
795	        height = item.get("height")
796	        proof = item.get("proof")
797	        if not _is_int(height) or not isinstance(proof, dict):
798	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
799	        if height < 0 or height >= len(blocks):
800	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
801	        block = blocks[height]
802	        if block.height != height:
803	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
804	        # Pending tips never carry trustworthy proofs.
805	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
806	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
807	
808	        tx_id = proof.get("tx_id")
809	        index = proof.get("index")
810	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id) or not _is_int(index):
811	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
812	        # The item height and the proof document's own fields must agree with
813	        # the candidate block they claim inclusion in.
814	        if proof.get("height") != height or proof.get("block_hash") != block.block_hash:
815	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
816	        if proof.get("merkle_root") != block.merkle_root:
817	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
818	        if index < 0 or index >= len(block.transactions):
819	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
820	        if block.transactions[index].tx_id != tx_id:
821	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
822	
823	        key = (height, tx_id)
824	        if key in seen:
825	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
826	        seen.add(key)
827	
828	        if not crypto.verify_merkle_proof(
829	            tx_id,
830	            proof.get("siblings"),
831	            block.merkle_root,
832	            block.block_hash,
833	            block.block_hash,
834	        ):
835	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
836	        verified.append(tx_id)
837	    return sorted(verified)
838	
839	
840	def _verify_state_proofs(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
841	    """Verify every account-state proof against the bundle's state anchor.
842	
843	    The anchor's confirmed transactions determine the ascending account set;
844	    each proof's ``account`` must belong to it and its ``index`` must be the
845	    account's position in that ordering. ``height`` + ``account`` pairs must
846	    be unique. Every proof is then checked with
847	    :func:`crypto.verify_account_proof` against the bundle's ``state_root``,
848	    ``state_height`` and ``state_block_hash``; any failure — an illegal
849	    direction or hash, a forged leaf, an illegal self-pair, a malformed
850	    sibling path — is a proof failure. Returns the verified accounts sorted
851	    ascending.
852	    """
853	    height = bundle["state_height"]
854	    # The account set of the anchor height: every account touched by a
855	    # confirmed transaction up to and including the anchor block, ascending.
856	    accounts: set[str] = set()
857	    for block in blocks[: height + 1]:
858	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
859	            continue
860	        for tx in block.transactions:
861	            accounts.add(tx.sender)
862	            accounts.add(tx.recipient)
863	    position = {account: index for index, account in enumerate(sorted(accounts))}
864	
865	    verified: list[str] = []
866	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
867	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
868	        proof = item["proof"]
869	        account = proof["account"]
870	        expected = position.get(account)
871	        # An account outside the anchor's set, or an index that is not the
872	        # account's ascending position (including out-of-range), is a proof
873	        # failure.
874	        if expected is None or proof["index"] != expected:
875	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
876	        key = (item["height"], account)
877	        if key in seen:
878	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
879	        seen.add(key)
880	        if not crypto.verify_account_proof(
881	            proof,
882	            bundle["state_root"],
883	            height,
884	            bundle["state_block_hash"],
885	        ):
886	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
887	        verified.append(account)
888	    return sorted(verified)

980	    order ``source, request_id, mode, expires_at, anchor, blocks, tip,
981	    attestation``); ``expected_anchor`` is the caller-pinned
982	    ``{height, block_hash}`` the first page's anchor must strictly equal;
983	    ``trust`` is the local trust document applied to every page.
984	
985	    The pages are re-verified in order: the first page is checked against
986	    ``expected_anchor``, and every later page's anchor must strictly equal the
987	    previous page's closed ``tip`` reduced to ``{height, block_hash}`` — which
988	    also rejects a height jump or a fork at the seam. Transaction ids must be
989	    unique across the whole batch, not just inside one page, and a pending
990	    block may only appear on the last page.
991

993	    success — ``anchor`` the pinned anchor of the first page, ``tip`` the last
994	    page's closed tip, ``pages`` the number of pages and
995	    ``verified_tx_ids`` ascending across every page — or
996	    ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` on failure with category one of
997	    ``input/auth/expired/integrity``. Never raises for malformed input.
998	    """
999	    current = time.time() if now is None else now
1000	    try:
1001	        if not isinstance(documents, list) or not documents:
1002	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1003	        # The pinned anchor is validated once up front so a malformed caller
1004	        # anchor is an input error even before the first page is inspected.
1005	        anchor = _validate_range_anchor(expected_anchor)
1006	        _validate_range_trust(trust)
1007	        pages = len(documents)

1014	            # _verify_range_page itself rejects a page whose anchor does not
1015	            # strictly equal ``expected`` — the first page's pinned anchor and
1016	            # every later page's previous tip — so a broken seam or a height
1017	            # jump surfaces as integrity here.
1018	            page_anchor, tip, page_tx_ids = _verify_range_page(
1019	                document, expected, trust, current
1020	            )
1021	            if first_anchor is None:
1022	                first_anchor = page_anchor

1024	            # one re-verified tail.
1025	            duplicates = seen_tx_ids.intersection(page_tx_ids)
1026	            if duplicates:
1027	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1028	            seen_tx_ids.update(page_tx_ids)
1029	            verified_ids.extend(page_tx_ids)

1033	            if tip["status"] == STATUS_PENDING and position != pages - 1:

1041	        # crash the verifying process.
1042	        return {"ok": False, "error": ERR_INPUT}

1044	        "ok": True,
1045	        "anchor": first_anchor,
1046	        "tip": last_tip,
1047	        "pages": pages,
1048	        "verified_tx_ids": sorted(verified_ids),

1055	    """Verify one range page, returning ``(anchor, tip, verified_tx_ids)``.

1058	    :func:`verify_range_exports` (a batch chaining each page's tip into the
1059	    next page's expected anchor). Raises :class:`_Failure` with the public
1060	    error category on every defect.
1061	    """
1062	    anchor = _validate_range_export_inputs(document, expected_anchor, trust)

1065	    if document["anchor"] != expected_anchor:
1066	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

1135	def _validate_range_trust(trust: object) -> None:
1136	    """Structural validation of the trust document's ``sources``/``allowlist``.
1137	
1138	    Mirrors the bundle verifier's trust rules; a ``genesis_hash`` is not
1139	    required here because the caller pins the range anchor directly. The
1140	    optional GET /v1/trust ``source_key_history`` mapping is validated too:
1141	    each source maps to a non-empty ascending array of
1142	    ``{version, public_key, activated_event_id}`` items whose versions are
1143	    dense from 1 with strictly ascending activation ids, both numeric fields
1144	    non-boolean positive integers and the public key 64 lowercase hex.
1145	    """
1146	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
1147	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1148	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
1149	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
1150	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1151	    for name, entry in sources.items():
1152	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
1153	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1154	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
1155	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1156	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
1157	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
1158	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
1159	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1160	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
1161	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
1162	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1163	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
1164	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
1165	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1166	    history = trust.get("source_key_history")
1167	    if history is not None:
1168	        if not isinstance(history, dict):
1169	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1170	        for name, entries in history.items():
1171	            if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
1172	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1173	            if not isinstance(entries, list) or not entries:
1174	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1175	            last_activated = None
1176	            for position, entry in enumerate(entries):
1177	                if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != set(
1178	                    _HISTORY_ENTRY_KEYS
1179	                ):
1180	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1181	                version = entry.get("version")
1182	                public_key = entry.get("public_key")
1183	                activated = entry.get("activated_event_id")
1184	                # Versions are dense from 1; both numeric fields are plain
1185	                # (non-boolean) positive integers.
1186	                if not _is_int(version) or version != position + 1:
1187	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1188	                if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
1189	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1190	                if not _is_int(activated) or activated < 1:
1191	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1192	                if last_activated is not None and activated <= last_activated:
1193	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1194	                last_activated = activated

1202	def _authenticate_range_export(document: dict, trust: dict, now: float) -> None:
1203	    """Check mode-specific source authorization and every deadline.
1204	
1205	    A ``plain`` export is only acceptable from an allowlisted source and must
1206	    carry ``attestation: null``. An ``attested`` export is authorized one of
1207	    two ways:
1208	
1209	    * the trust document carries a ``source_key_history`` mapping (the new
1210	      rule): the source must appear in the mapping — the historical public key
1211	      matching and signature verification happen by attestation version in
1212	      :func:`_verify_range_attestation`; the trust ``sources`` entry and its
1213	      deadline play no role, so a delivery signed under a since-rotated or
1214	      revoked key still authenticates as long as the document itself is
1215	      unexpired;
1216	    * the mapping is absent (the legacy rule): the source must be a
1217	      ``sources`` entry whose unexpired deadline is checked.
1218	
1219	    All deadlines are checked before any integrity work: an expired,
1220	    correctly-signed export is still unusable.
1221	    """
1222	    source = document["source"]
1223	    mode = document["mode"]
1224	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
1225	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
1226	    if mode == "plain":
1227	        if source not in allowlist:
1228	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1229	        # A plain export carrying an attestation is not a plain delivery.
1230	        if document["attestation"] is not None:
1231	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1232	    elif _has_key_history(trust):
1233	        # Historical-key authorization: the source (and later the attestation
1234	        # version) must resolve in the mapping; the current registry entry is
1235	        # deliberately not consulted.
1236	        if source not in trust["source_key_history"]:
1237	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1238	    elif source not in sources:
1239	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1240	
1241	    if document["expires_at"] <= now:
1242	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
1243	    if mode == "plain":
1244	        if allowlist[source] <= now:
1245	            raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
1246	    elif not _has_key_history(trust) and sources[source]["expires_at"] <= now:
1247	        # Legacy rule only: the pinned registry entry's own deadline applies.
1248	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)

1251	def _recompute_range_tail(anchor: dict, blocks_raw: list) -> list[Block]:
1252	    """Recompute and validate the delivered tail standalone from the anchor.
1253	
1254	    Mirrors the node's own range-tail rules: heights run consecutively from
1255	    ``anchor.height + 1``, the first ``prev_hash`` is the anchor hash and
1256	    later ones link internally, every transaction's tx_id and Ed25519
1257	    signature verifies, tx_ids are unique across the tail and ascending
1258	    inside each block, Merkle roots and block hashes recompute, and a pending
1259	    block may only sit at the tail tip. Every field is checked on the *raw*
1260	    JSON value; type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height,
1261	    non-positive or non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while
1262	    recomputation mismatches stay ``integrity``.
1263	    """
1264	    blocks: list[Block] = []
1265	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
1266	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(blocks_raw):
1267	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
1268	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1269	        height = block_raw.get("height")
1270	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
1271	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
1272	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
1273	        status = block_raw.get("status")
1274	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
1275	        # Same rule as the whole-chain recomputation: a height of the wrong
1276	        # type or sign is a field-type defect (input), never coerced.
1277	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
1278	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1279	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
1280	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1281	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
1282	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1283	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
1284	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1285	        if height != anchor["height"] + 1 + position:
1286	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1287	        expected_prev = (
1288	            anchor["block_hash"] if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
1289	        )
1290	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
1291	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1292	        if position < len(blocks_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
1293	            # A pending block may only sit at the tail tip.
1294	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1295	
1296	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
1297	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
1298	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
1299	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1300	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
1301	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
1302	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
1303	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
1304	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
1305	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
1306	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1307	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
1308	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1309	            # The raw amount must already be a non-boolean positive integer —
1310	            # never a coercible string, float or bool.
1311	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
1312	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1313	            if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
1314	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1315	            message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
1316	            tx_id = crypto.compute_tx_id(message)
1317	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
1318	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1319	            if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
1320	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1321	            if tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
1322	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1323	            seen_tx_ids.add(tx_id)
1324	            tx_ids.append(tx_id)
1325	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
1326	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1327	        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
1328	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1329	        recomputed = compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root)
1330	        if recomputed != block_hash:
1331	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1332	        # Parsed only after every raw field has checked out; never trusted for
1333	        # the comparison decisions above.
1334	        try:
1335	            blocks.append(Block.from_dict(block_raw))
1336	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
1337	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
1338	    return blocks

1359	def _verify_range_attestation(document: dict, trust: dict) -> None:
1360	    """Verify the attested export's Ed25519 signature under the pinned key.
1361	
1362	    Two rules, selected by the trust document:
1363	
1364	    * with ``source_key_history`` present, the attestation's ``version``
1365	      selects the source's historical public key; the source not appearing in
1366	      the mapping, or the attestation version not being one of its dense
1367	      versions, is an authorization failure (``auth``), as is a mismatch
1368	      between the attestation's ``public_key`` and that historical key. The
1369	      Ed25519 signature is then checked over the SHA-256 digest of the
1370	      canonical ``ledger-sync-range-v1`` message — a wrong signature is an
1371	      integrity failure. The attestation's version is already structurally
1372	      guaranteed to be a positive integer.
1373	    * without the mapping (legacy rule), the attestation's ``public_key``
1374	      must be exactly the key the trust document pins in ``sources`` for the
1375	      source (a mismatched credential is an authorization failure) and the
1376	      same signature check follows.
1377	    """
1378	    source = document["source"]
1379	    attestation = document["attestation"]
1380	    if _has_key_history(trust):
1381	        history = trust["source_key_history"].get(source)
1382	        if history is None:
1383	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1384	        version = attestation["version"]
1385	        # Versions are structurally guaranteed dense from 1, so a valid
1386	        # version simply indexes the ascending history.
1387	        if version < 1 or version > len(history):
1388	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1389	        pinned = history[version - 1]["public_key"]
1390	        if attestation["public_key"] != pinned:
1391	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1392	    else:
1393	        pinned = trust.get("sources", {})[source]["public_key"]
1394	        if attestation["public_key"] != pinned:
1395	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1396	    message = attested_range_message(
1397	        source,
1398	        document["request_id"],
1399	        document["expires_at"],
1400	        document["anchor"],
1401	        document["blocks"],
1402	        document["tip"],
1403	    )
1404	    digest = hashlib.sha256(message).digest()
1405	    if not crypto.verify_signature(pinned, digest, attestation["signature"]):
1406	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

"""Offline light-client verification of externally supplied proof bundles.

A proof bundle lets a client verify ledger responses without trusting the
serving node or holding any chain state:

    bundle = {
        "source": str,
        "expires_at": int,            # Unix seconds
        "response": object,           # the attested response object
        "candidate": [...],           # full block list starting at genesis
        "proofs": [                   # optional Merkle inclusion proofs
            {"height": int, "proof": {height, tx_id, index, merkle_root,
                                      block_hash, siblings}},
            ...
        ],
        # Optional account-state extension: all four fields are either present
        # together or absent together, and state_proofs is a non-empty list.
        "state_root": str,            # 64 lowercase hex, anchored state root
        "state_height": int,          # confirmed anchor block height
        "state_block_hash": str,      # 64 lowercase hex anchor block hash
        "state_proofs": [             # account-state inclusion proofs
            {"height": int, "proof": {account, balance,
                                      confirmed_transactions, index,
                                      state_root, height, block_hash,
                                      siblings}},
            ...
        ],
        "signature": str,             # optional Ed25519 signature hex
    }

The local trust document pins the genesis block hash and records, per source,
an optional Ed25519 public key with its own expiry, plus an allowlist of
sources accepted without signatures:

    trust = {
        "genesis_hash": "<64 lowercase hex chars>",
        "sources": {source: {"public_key": hex, "expires_at": int}},
        "allowlist": {source: expires_at_int},
    }

Verification, in order:

1. **input** — bundle and trust must have the documented shape; every numeric
   field must be a plain (non-boolean) integer.
2. **auth** — the source must be trusted (a ``sources`` entry or the
   ``allowlist``). A source with a public key must sign the bundle; a bundle
   carrying a signature for a key-less source, or an unsigned bundle from a
   non-allowlisted source, fails.
3. **expired** — neither the bundle deadline nor the trust entry's deadline
   may have passed (``expires_at <= now`` counts as expired).
4. **integrity** — the signature (when required) is verified over
   Ed25519(sha256(sorted-compact UTF-8 JSON of the bundle without
   ``signature``)); the candidate chain is recomputed from the pinned genesis
   (heights, prev_hash linkage, every transaction's tx_id and Ed25519
   signature, unique tx_ids, Merkle roots, block hashes, pending-only-at-tip)
   and the response's descriptor fields are checked against the recomputed
   tip descriptor ``S``.
5. **proof** — every proof must be unique, its tx_id/height/index and block
   fields must agree with the candidate block, the Merkle path must verify
   under the existing rules, and its block must not be the pending tip. When
   the state extension is present, its anchor (``state_height`` /
   ``state_block_hash``) must name a confirmed candidate block (integrity) and
   every state proof must agree with both anchor heights, the state root and
   the anchor hash; each account must sit at its ``index`` in the ascending
   account set of the anchor height's confirmed transactions, ``height`` +
   ``account`` pairs must be unique, and every proof must pass
   ``crypto.verify_account_proof`` against the bundle's anchors.

On success :func:`verify_bundle` returns
``{"ok": True, "source", "S", "verified_tx_ids"}`` — plus
``"verified_accounts"`` (ascending) when the state extension was verified —
on failure ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
``input/auth/expired/integrity/proof``.

:func:`verify_range_export` verifies one exported incremental range delivery
(the ``GET /v1/forks/sync/range/export`` document, top-level key order
``source, request_id, mode, expires_at, anchor, blocks, tip, attestation``)
offline against a caller-pinned expected anchor and the local trust document.
The expected anchor must strictly equal the document's ``anchor``; the
delivered tail is recomputed standalone from that anchor (consecutive
heights, prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures,
unique and block-ascending tx_ids, Merkle roots, block hashes,
pending-only-at-tip) and the closed ``tip`` summary must recompute. A
``plain`` export must come from an unexpired ``allowlist`` entry and carry
``attestation: null``. An ``attested`` export is authenticated by key
version: when the trust document carries a ``source_key_history`` mapping,
the attestation's ``version`` selects that source's historical public key
(which must equal the attestation's ``public_key``); an unknown source or
version, or a mismatched key, is ``auth`` and a signature that fails to
verify is ``integrity`` — so an export signed under a since-rotated key
stays verifiable. A trust document without ``source_key_history`` keeps the
legacy rule: the source must be an unexpired ``trust.sources`` entry whose
pinned key matches the attestation and verifies the Ed25519 signature over
the SHA-256 digest of the canonical ``ledger-sync-range-v1`` message.
Failures map to ``input`` (structure), ``auth`` (authorization), ``expired``
(deadlines) and ``integrity`` (anchor/chain/signature); nothing is raised.
Success returns ``{"ok": True, "source", "request_id", "mode", "anchor",
"tip", "verified_tx_ids"}`` with ``verified_tx_ids`` ascending.

:func:`verify_range_exports` verifies an ordered, non-empty batch of such
range deliveries as one continuous chain. The first page's anchor must equal
the caller-pinned ``expected_anchor``; every later page's anchor must equal
the previous page's closed tip's ``{height, block_hash}``. Each page is
re-verified under the same input/auth/expired/integrity rules, transaction
ids are unique across the whole batch, and a pending block may only appear on
the last page — a broken anchor, a height jump, a duplicate transaction or any
block after a pending one is an ``integrity`` failure. Success returns
``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "pages", "verified_tx_ids"}`` with ``tip``
the last page's tip, ``pages`` the page count and ``verified_tx_ids``
ascending; failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one
of ``input/auth/expired/integrity``.

:func:`verify_header_page` verifies one signed ``GET /v1/chain/headers``
page offline. The document has the exact top-level key order
``anchor, headers, tip, auth``: a closed ``{height, block_hash}`` anchor, an
ascending list of ``{height, prev_hash, merkle_root, block_hash, status}``
headers (no transactions), the chain descriptor S and an
``{key_version, signature}`` envelope. The caller pins both the anchor and
the tip hash; ``trust.audit_signers`` supplies the public key selected by
``key_version``. Key-order/type defects are ``input``; an unknown key
version or a failed Ed25519 verification over
``SHA256(UTF8("ledger-headers-v1") || canonical_json(document without
auth))`` is ``auth``; an anchor/tip mismatch, a recomputed header hash or
prev_hash link mismatch, a non-consecutive height, or a pending header
anywhere but the chain tail is ``integrity``. An empty page is valid only
when its anchor is the pinned tip. Success returns
``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "verified_block_hashes"}``; nothing is
raised for malformed input.

:func:`verify_header_pages` verifies an ordered, non-empty batch of such
signed header pages as one continuous chain. Every page is re-verified
under the exact :func:`verify_header_page` contract (key order, types,
signer history, domain signature, recomputed header hashes); the first
page's anchor must strictly equal the caller-pinned ``anchor`` and every
later page's anchor must equal the previous page's last header's
``{height, block_hash}``, so heights and prev_hash links continue across
the page seams and a missing, duplicated or reordered page breaks the
chain. Every page's ``tip`` descriptor must be field-for-field identical
and name the caller-pinned ``tip_hash``; the last page must reach that
tip. A non-final page's headers may never be empty — an empty page is
only ever valid as the batch's last page with its anchor being the tip —
and a pending header may only be the very last header of the whole batch,
so any page after a pending header is an ``integrity`` failure. Success
returns ``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "pages",
"verified_block_hashes"}`` with ``pages`` the page count and the hashes
in chain order (the anchor itself is not a header and is not included);
failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
``input`` (array/parameter shape, key order, types), ``auth`` (unknown
key version or a failed signature) and ``integrity`` (anchor, tip, hash,
link, pagination or pending-position defects). Nothing is raised.

:func:`verify_header_locator_page` verifies one signed
``POST /v1/chain/headers/locate`` page offline. The document is the same
fixed-order signed page as :func:`verify_header_page`
(``anchor, headers, tip, auth``); instead of one caller-pinned anchor the
caller passes the original ``locators`` list (1-64 ``{height, block_hash}``
items, heights non-boolean non-negative integers, strictly descending and
unique, hashes 64 lowercase hex). The document's own anchor must be one of
those locators — its position in the supplied list is returned as
``matched_index`` (starting at 0) — and every other rule is the
:func:`verify_header_page` rule: the signer version resolves in
``trust.audit_signers`` and verifies the domain-prefixed Ed25519 signature,
the header hashes and prev_hash links recompute from the anchor and the
descriptor names the caller-pinned ``tip_hash``. Bad parameters or list
shape/key order/types are ``input``; an unknown key version or a failed
signature is ``auth``; an anchor absent from the locator list, a broken
header chain or a tip mismatch is ``integrity``. Success returns
``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "matched_index",
"verified_block_hashes"}``; failure returns only ``{"ok": False,
"error": category}`` and nothing is raised.

:func:`advance_headers` durably checkpoints a verified header-page batch to
``path``. The file is one compact UTF-8 JSON document (non-ASCII written
unescaped, one trailing newline) with the exact top-level key order
``v, generation, anchor, tip, steps, hash``: ``v`` is 1, ``generation`` is a
non-boolean positive integer incremented once per successful advance,
``anchor`` is the first batch's pinned ``{height, block_hash}`` anchor (key
order ``height, block_hash``), ``tip`` is the latest chain descriptor S,
``steps`` is a non-empty array of ``{tip_hash, trust, documents}`` items (one
per advance, nested key orders unchanged) and ``hash`` is the SHA-256 of the
canonical (sorted, compact) JSON of the document with ``hash`` removed. The
first use of ``path`` requires a legal ``anchor``; later advances accept
``None`` (continue from the stored tip) or the stored tip's
``{height, block_hash}``. Verification itself is :func:`verify_header_pages`
unchanged against the caller-pinned ``tip_hash``. The new tip may never drop
in height; at the same height only the same ``block_hash`` moving from
``pending`` to ``confirmed`` is accepted — anything else is an ``integrity``
failure. Re-submitting the exact last batch (same ``tip_hash``, ``trust`` and
``documents``) is idempotent: it verifies but neither bumps the generation
nor touches the file. Loading strictly replays every stored step (shape,
hash, per-batch verification and tip monotonicity) and checks the stored
tip; any mismatch is a ``state`` failure and the file is never truncated or
rebuilt. Same-path advances share one lock and the new file is atomically
replaced into place; a failed write restores the original bytes. Success
returns ``{"ok": True, "generation", "tip"}``; failure returns only
``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
``input/auth/integrity/state/io`` and nothing is raised.

:func:`advance` durably checkpoints a verified batch to ``path``. The
checkpoint file is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with the exact declared key
order ``generation, anchor, tip, context, state_hash`` and a single trailing
newline (non-ASCII written unescaped); ``generation`` starts at 1 and
increments per successful advance, ``anchor``/``tip`` are the batch's pinned
anchor and closed tip, ``context`` has the exact key order
``verified_at, trust, documents, verified_tx_ids`` (the ``now`` at verification,
the trust document and the re-verifiable batch verbatim) and ``state_hash`` is
the SHA-256 of the canonical (sorted, compact) JSON of the other four fields.
The first advance requires a legal ``anchor``; later advances accept ``None``
(continue from the stored tip) or the stored tip's ``{height, block_hash}``.
Verification itself is :func:`verify_range_exports` unchanged. Same-path
advances share one lock and the new file is atomically replaced into place; a
failed verification never bumps the generation. An existing checkpoint is
strictly reloaded (key order, types, state hash and a context replay at its
``verified_at``); any mismatch is a ``state`` failure and the file is never
truncated or rebuilt. Failures return only ``{"ok": False, "error":
category}`` with category one of
``input/auth/expired/integrity/state/io``; success appends the new
``generation`` as the final result key.

Every successful :func:`advance` also maintains a generation-history sidecar
at ``path + ".history"``: one compact UTF-8 JSON document (same serialization
rules as the checkpoint) with the exact top-level key order
``v, base, records, head``. ``v`` is 1; ``base`` is ``{generation, hash}``
naming the generation *before* the first retained record; each record is
``{checkpoint, prev, hash}`` where ``checkpoint`` is the persisted five-key
checkpoint document, ``prev`` is the previous record's hash (the first
record's is ``base.hash``) and ``hash`` is
``SHA256(ASCII(prev) || canonical_json(checkpoint))``; ``head`` is the last
record's hash. Record generations run consecutively from
``base.generation + 1``. A fresh path starts from ``base = {0, Z}`` (Z = 64
zeros); a pre-existing generation-``g`` checkpoint without a sidecar is
treated as ``base = {g-1, Z}`` with that checkpoint as the first record, and
later advances append. Both files are written under the same per-path lock as
one transaction: an ``io`` failure restores the original bytes best-effort
(a failed compensation surfaces as ``state`` on the next read); crash
atomicity across the two files is not guaranteed.

:func:`history` reads (and prunes) the sidecar. ``history(path)`` returns
``{"ok", "base", "record", "head", "kept"}`` with ``record`` the last
generation's record and ``kept`` null; ``generation=`` selects one retained
generation (an absent one is a ``state`` failure). ``keep=n`` (mutually
exclusive with ``generation``; both must be non-boolean positive integers)
retains only the last ``min(n, count)`` records: when nothing is pruned the
file's bytes are untouched, otherwise ``base`` becomes the last pruned
record's ``{generation, hash}`` and the sidecar is rewritten (the checkpoint
file itself never changes). Loading replays every retained generation —
shape, state hash, context replay and anchor continuity — so any tampering
is a ``state`` failure; a missing or unreadable sidecar is ``io``.

:func:`export_history` exports the retained sidecar pages as signed,
offline-verifiable page documents. ``export_history(path, key, after=None,
limit=50, trust_path=None)`` strictly reloads both the checkpoint and its
sidecar under the shared per-path lock and returns one page with the exact key
order ``base, records, next, head, checkpoint, auth``: ``base``/``records``
are the sidecar's own documents (nested key orders unchanged), ``head`` the
sidecar head, ``checkpoint`` the persisted five-key checkpoint (identical to
the last retained record's), ``next`` the page's last record generation when
another page follows or ``null`` on the final page, and ``auth`` is
``{public_key, signature}`` where the Ed25519 signature is made by the 64-hex
seed ``key`` over the SHA-256 of the canonical (sorted, compact,
unescaped-non-ASCII) JSON of the page with ``auth`` removed. ``after`` is
``None`` (start after ``base``) or a non-boolean non-negative integer naming
either ``base.generation`` or a non-last retained generation; ``limit`` is a
non-boolean integer in 1..200. Bad arguments are ``input``, a missing or
unreadable file ``io`` and a corrupt checkpoint/sidecar or unmatched cursor
``state``. With ``trust_path`` set to a signer log (see
:func:`history_trust`), the log is strictly loaded first (a missing log is
``io`` and a corrupt one ``state``) and the page is truncated to the longest
prefix, starting at the cursor, whose checkpoints all carry the same key
active at their ``verified_at``: it stops just before the first record that
would straddle an authorization boundary and sets ``next`` (non-null) so the
following page continues there. The seed ``key`` must derive to the public
key covering that whole span — an unknown or revoked covering key is an
``auth`` failure. A page ending exactly at the retained tail still closes
with ``next: null``.

:func:`verify_history` verifies an ordered, non-empty list of such pages
offline against one pinned 64-hex Ed25519 ``public_key``. Every page must have
the exact key order and nested types; ``base``, ``head``, ``checkpoint`` and
the signing public key must be identical on every page; each Ed25519 signature
must verify over the auth-less canonical page digest. Records must run
consecutively from ``base.generation + 1`` and link across page seams through
each page's ``next`` (a non-final page's ``next`` is its last record
generation), every record hash is recomputed and every checkpoint is replayed
(state hash plus the stored batch context) with anchor continuity. The final
page alone carries ``next: null``, its last record's hash must equal ``head``
and its checkpoint must equal the page checkpoint; missing, duplicate or
reordered pages and any tampering are rejected. Success is ``{"ok": True}``;
failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
``input`` (structure/types), ``auth`` (pinned key or signature) and
``integrity`` (chaining, pagination or checkpoint replay); nothing is raised.

:func:`verify_history_trust` verifies the same pages against a signer
rotation/revocation log instead of one pinned page key, so each page's
``auth.public_key`` may differ. The ``trust`` document has the exact key
order ``root, records, head``: ``root`` is a 64-hex Ed25519 key that must
equal the pinned ``root`` argument; every non-empty record has the exact key
order ``at, key, status, prev, signature`` with ``at`` a plain
(non-boolean) positive strictly-ascending integer, ``key``/``prev`` 64
lowercase hex, ``status`` exactly ``active``/``revoked`` and ``signature``
128 lowercase hex. The first ``prev`` is 64 zeros, every later one is the
previous record's canonical-JSON SHA-256 and ``head`` is the last record's
hash; each certificate is the root key's Ed25519 signature over the
SHA-256 of the record's canonical JSON with ``signature`` removed. An
``active`` record authorizes ``key`` from its ``at`` until the next record;
a ``revoked`` one withdraws it until a later ``active``. A page must name
the single key active at every checkpoint ``verified_at`` it carries — a
page straddling an authorization boundary is rejected — and its signature
must verify over the auth-less canonical page digest. All page structure,
chaining, pagination and checkpoint-replay rules stay identical to
:func:`verify_history`. Failures map to ``input`` (missing/extra/reordered
keys, wrong types or hex), ``auth`` (root mismatch, a bad certificate or
page signature, an unknown or revoked page key) and ``integrity`` (``at``
not ascending, a bad ``prev``/``head``, a boundary crossing, or any
record/pagination/checkpoint-replay defect); nothing is raised and success
is ``{"ok": True}``.

:func:`history_trust` persists such a signer log at its own file path.
``history_trust(path)`` strictly loads and returns the ``{root, records,
head}`` document; a missing file is an ``io`` failure and any damaged log a
``state`` failure. ``history_trust(path, root_seed, at, key, status)``
appends one root-signed certificate — the four update fields are all required
or all absent — with ``root_seed`` a 64-hex Ed25519 seed (its public key is
the log root), ``at`` a non-boolean positive integer, ``key`` a 64-hex public
key and ``status`` ``active``/``revoked``. A fresh log must open with
``active``; ``at`` must strictly ascend; a ``revoked`` entry must name the
currently active key; re-appending the current tail's ``at``/``key``/
``status`` is idempotent. A seed whose root does not match the existing log
is ``auth``; bad argument shapes are ``input``; read-missing and read/write
``io``. The file uses the same compact-UTF-8/unescaped/single-trailing-
newline serialization and atomic per-path-locked replace as the checkpoint
files, and a failed write restores the original bytes best-effort.
